doc: The frozen I60 instrument: the replacement of I22's rejected catalog (BUILD_PLAN §3 row I60; §4 I22, whose kill criterion, threshold and exit it inherits). It fixes, before anything runs, the denominator (strata, site rule, operators with exact rewrite rules, the mutants), the predicted laws of every mutant by one mechanical rule, the structural class of every mutant (which decision paths can see it), the kill criterion (K1, K2 with its three conditions, masked obstructions, law-scoped errors), the replay semantics, the equivalence definition, the reporting and the adjudication protocol. BUILD_PLAN names spec/M2/preregistration.json; a prereg commit may only add files under spec/M2/lib/ (holon/audit/prereg.py), hence the path. It is the only target-facing input of holon/mutate/. Contract: the docstring of tests_m2/test_mutation_adequacy_i60.py. Every value was computed at the prereg from the pinned checkout and the committed artifacts pinned in 'pins' (computation); no mutant was extracted, projected, decided or replayed (each was only compiled, items 6 and 7). The sign-off and the equivalence verdicts are delegated to independent fresh agents (adjudication): nothing runs before both are committed.

replaces.rule: I22's own contract (the tests_m2/test_mutation_adequacy.py docstring, preregistered at f8fa447; BUILD_PLAN §3 row I60 restates it): 'If the human rejects the catalog, nothing runs and a replacement is preregistered under a new key.' The human delegated the sign-off to independent fresh agents (docs/iterations/I22.md); both lenses declined it. The I22 panel's verdicts (docs/iterations/I22_equivalence_panel.json) adjudicate another catalog and are not reused.

findings.F-B1 (fairness, blocking): the in-scope: Fixed. Stratum A is the coverage-certified scope: the functions and modifiers the I19 walker reaches from all 33 actions of the adopted rollup document (the set gen/M2/coverage.json counts: 422 statements, 419 extracted, 12 debt), plus every function of the two header codec libraries, plus the Go codec file the M2 diagram adopts. Stratum B is every other Go codec file of a committed extracted document. No rule mentions a law; the 11 out-of-scope I22 sites (claimReward's delete at Rollup.sol:675; cmp at :211, :501, :510, :519, :554, :815; cursor reads at :192, :193, :212, :686) are all in stratum A.
findings.F-A1 (fairness): part of the outcome was: Fixed. Every mutant carries its structural class (structural), computed by a stated rule before freezing; structural_counts states the ceiling (103 of 192 stratum-A mutants are reachable).
findings.F-A2 (fairness): predicted sets were not: Fixed. One rule for every operator (predicted): M0 laws whose statement calls a role in the mutant's edges (dec_go implies ok_go); M1x laws whose recorded cone names one of its actions; M2 laws whose DERIVATION entry points include one of its actions, laws derived only on the mutant included.
findings.F-A3 (fairness): cmp_boundary used 'any': Fixed. The same rule for every operator; K1 and K2 by laws outside the predicted set are reported per operator as unpredicted obstructions, never counted.
findings.F-A4 (fairness) and S-B1 (soundness, blo: Fixed. K2 is per law and needs (a) the law's own decided input changed, (b) the generator that proved it at baseline completed on the mutant and Bend rejected the proof, (c) a code-level localized falsification in the law's candidate space; (a)+(b) without (c) is proof_lost_unwitnessed, never a kill. A timeout, LG.Unsupported or a generator returning None is a law-level error. A K1-only rate is reported.
findings.F-A5 (fairness): laws derived only on th: Fixed. A law absent at baseline and derived on the mutant counts as baseline UNKNOWN for K1, with two-sided replay and its basis span inside a mutated function; a re-derived law is first matched to a baseline law by (rule, subform, basis span).
findings.F-A7 (fairness): the rate is driven by c: Fixed. Rates per stratum, per operator and per law family; duplicate candidate groups (same operator, same statement) are adjudicated by the panel and a deduplicated rate is reported.
findings.F-A8 (fairness): decoders were never mut: Fixed. Operators mload_offset and shr_width (Solidity get*) and go_slice_offset (Go getter slice bounds).
findings.F-A9 (fairness): the Go scope rationale: Fixed. Go stratum A is the codec file the M2 diagram adopts (common/batch/batch_header.go: the CODEC edges enc_go_v0, enc_go_v1, dec_go and the predicate ok_go of gen/M2/diagram/morph_header.json); stratum B is every other file that holds an I18-recognized codec (go.codecs encoders, decoders or predicates) of a committed extracted document, measured and reported with no threshold.
findings.S-B2 (soundness, blocking): the error cl: Fixed. Errors are scoped to laws: a failed step marks only the laws it decides (or whose witness it replays) as error. A mutant is killed iff some predicted law satisfies K1 or K2 on a path that completed; it is error iff it is not killed and some predicted law is undecided by an error. Errors are counted per step.
findings.S-A1 (soundness): structural ceiling; a: Fixed. Structural classes are recorded; nothing here claims a law decides on the extracted model where it does not (M1x is decided on m1_view; M2 site laws on the hand model; M2 width laws on the extracted model, which has no Reach predicate).
findings.S-A2 (soundness): obstructions behind a: Fixed. A masked obstruction is a model hit of a baseline-REFUTED predicted law that replays on the mutant code and not on the original: reported as a separate rate, never a kill; survivor class 'masked'.
findings.S-A3 (soundness): the replay panic/error: Fixed (replay.semantics): an error or revert that is the function's declared value is not a violation; a panic the declared meaning does not map falsifies the claim; a reverted trace step is a no-op.
findings.S-A4 (soundness): K1 replay mechanics un: Fixed. The replay harness is a deliverable (replay): by claim, exact field values, through the tree's own code; up to 16 model hits enumerated in candidate order; a Bend-checked counter-law for the recorded witness; construction tests against I16's committed real outputs and planted controls.
findings.S-A5 (soundness): 'replays on both' was: Fixed. A witness that replays on both versions is a baseline finding (whitepaper §9.6), never a kill and never an extraction defect.
findings.S-A6 (soundness): equivalence wording, c: Fixed (equivalence): Rollup is the deployed contract the libraries and the inherited contracts compile into; Go is the package's exported API. Contradicted verdicts are reported with the rate recomputed with them reversed; the adjudicator is recorded (delegated panel).
findings.S-A7 (soundness): minor rewrite-rule poi: Fixed. A dropped statement becomes {} followed by exactly the newline characters of the replaced range; the mirrored comparisons are an operator.
findings.S-A9 (soundness): unpredicted obstructio: Fixed. Re-derived laws are matched by (rule, subform, basis span); unpredicted obstructions are reported per operator, and a detection rate counts every localized obstruction (killed, unpredicted or masked).
findings.S-A10 (soundness): determinism checks la: Fixed. A run --check disagreement is an error of the affected laws, reported; it voids carrying for them.
Limitations that stay (preregistered, no: M1x laws are decided on I20's window view m1_view (the hand abstraction minus the requires no extracted check of the same action overlaps by span). No operator here adds or removes a check reach, so the view, and every M1x status, is carried by construction: 51 stratum-A mutants are abstraction-carried. A decision path that consumes extracted effects for the rollup laws does not exist at this pipeline.

M2 SORT-site laws are decided on the hand model; SORT-width laws on the extracted model, which has no Reach predicate, so they can only be UNKNOWN (docs/iterations/I20.md, Not done). No M2 law can move.
L_dom_hdr, L_par_hdr_v2 and L_par_hdr_ssvh are REFUTED at baseline: what they see is measured as masked obstructions, never as kills.
The Solidity getters (mload_offset, shr_width) feed no projected op: the projection reads the stored Header fields, not how Rollup computed them. They are measured, not excluded.
Stratum B has no decision path: no adopted document reads node/types, the genesis encoder or batch_data. It is measured with no threshold.
The operator patterns are I22's (PutUint64 only, not PutUint16/32; a dropped length check whose body returns one of the I18 non-nil error forms), recomputed on the new scope.
Equivalence is over Rollup's public entry points: a library user that is not deployed (a mock) is out of it.

Whitepaper §9.5 lists 'wrong masks' among A1's misimplementations. No in-scope file of either stratum holds a literal bit mask (no Yul and(), no Go & with a constant, no 0xff literal outside comments; checked on the pinned bytes at the prereg), so no mask operator exists here; shl_width and shr_width are the nearest form. A mask operator is added when a scope holds a mask.
Rewrites are single-site and single-token (first-order mutants); interactions of two faults are not measured.

pins.why: The instrument reads I20's merged code and outputs (the reviewers' S-A8: the I22 instrument cited unmerged I20 code). holon_commit is the project-branch commit the values below were computed at (I20 merged, 04e2293); files maps every committed artifact the computation read to its sha256 there. A later change of one of them is a note, never a reason to recompute the catalog.

computation: 1. Target. config/holon.json replay.morph = /root/work/morph, a clean checkout at 3e44e795586af3e11285b603ab642c67823add51 (git status empty); the OpenZeppelin units come from replay.sol_deps/node_modules (pinned by replay.sol_deps_sha256). The holon tree is the project branch at pins.holon_commit (04e2293, I20 merged). Every in-scope file's sha256 (in_scope.files) equals the sha256 the committed extracted documents record for the same input: spec/M2/facts/morph_rollup.extracted.json extraction.inputs for the Solidity units, the Go documents' extraction.inputs for the Go files.

2. Solidity scope (stratum A). holon.frontends.solidity.transitions.walk_contract on spec/M2/lib/extract_rollup.json with the pinned solc (compile_sources with storageLayout): Collector.reached holds 92 FunctionDefinitions and ModifierDefinitions (Rollup 44, BatchHeaderCodecV0 23, BatchHeaderCodecV1 2, PausableUpgradeable 9, OwnableUpgradeable 8, Initializable 4, AddressUpgradeable 1, ContextUpgradeable 1); coverage_document over the same walk gives statements 422, extracted 419, 12 debt entries, 0 unaccounted, as gen/M2/coverage.json. The two codec functions no action reaches (BatchHeaderCodecV0.getParentBatchHash, BatchHeaderCodecV1.getLastBlockNumber) are added: 94 functions. Per action (predicted.actions): the closure over Identifier, IdentifierPath, MemberAccess and ModifierInvocation references from each of the 33 actions; the union of the 33 closures is exactly the 92 reached.

3. Go strata. gen/M2/diagram/morph_header.json is the only M2 diagram with CODEC edges (CODEC.dec_go, CODEC.enc_go_v0, CODEC.enc_go_v1, CODEC.enc_sol) and domain predicates (ok_go, ok_sol); their facts (facts/morph_header.json) cite one Go source file, common/batch/batch_header.go: stratum A (every function). The committed Go documents (spec/M2/facts/morph_{batch,blob,derivation,genesis,nodetypes}.go.extracted.json) list go.codecs encoders, decoders and predicates in 12 files; the 11 besides stratum A form stratum B: common/batch/{batch_cache,batch_data,batch_storage,encoding}.go, node/derivation/{batch_info,blob_type}.go, node/types/{batch_header,consensus_message,converter}.go, ops/l2-genesis/morph-chain-ops/genesis/{batch,config}.go. Seven of them hold a site.

4. Sites. Each operator's pattern (operators.<op>.pattern) was matched on the solc compact AST of every in-scope Solidity function and modifier body (the Yul AST of its inline assembly included; offsets are byte offsets of the unit) and with go/ast on every function of every in-scope Go file. Sites: Solidity mstore_offset 11, shl_width 6, drop_delete 7, swap_cursor 12, cmp_boundary 23, cmp_boundary_mirror 15, mload_offset 11, shr_width 5 (90); Go stratum A putuint64_offset 7, copy_offset 14, drop_len_check 4, go_slice_offset 12 (37); Go stratum B putuint64_offset 4, copy_offset 4, drop_len_check 11, go_slice_offset 12 (31). A Solidity site in an OpenZeppelin unit is mutated in a scratch copy of sol_deps.

5. Mutants. One per site and variant of its rewrite: stratum A 192 (mstore_offset 22, shl_width 12, drop_delete 7, swap_cursor 12, cmp_boundary 23, cmp_boundary_mirror 15, mload_offset 22, shr_width 9 (getVersion's shr(248) has only -8), putuint64_offset 14, copy_offset 28, drop_len_check 4, go_slice_offset 24); stratum B 51 generated, 1 stillborn (item 7), 50 kept. offset/length are the replaced byte range, original its text, replacement the new text, line/col (1-based) its first byte, function the enclosing function (the walker's name for Solidity, the go/ssa name for Go), mutant_sha256 the sha256 of the whole mutated file. Every replacement keeps the file's line count. Ids per stratum (A001.., B001..) in operator_order, then in_scope.order, then offset, then variant_order.

6. Solidity compilation: solc 0.8.24 standard JSON on contracts/contracts/l1/rollup/Rollup.sol (base path the checkout, include path sol_deps/node_modules, optimizer off, evmVersion cancun, metadata bytecodeHash none and appendCBOR false) with the mutated unit given as content: all 122 Solidity mutants compile. Six leave Rollup's deployed bytecode unchanged (tce): A110, A111, A112, A113 (mload offsets of getParentBatchHash and getLastBlockNumber) and A121, A122 (shr widths of getLastBlockNumber), functions Rollup never calls. Every other Solidity mutant changes it.

7. Go compilation: go build of the mutated package in a scratch copy of the checkout's go.work modules (GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOPROXY=off, go1.24.7): every stratum-A mutant (70) and 50 of 51 stratum-B mutants build. Stillborn: the drop_len_check at common/batch/encoding.go:21 (the dropped body was fmt's only use: '"fmt" imported and not used'); it is listed in stillborn and is no mutant.

8. Edges, actions, predicted sets and structural classes by the rules of roles, predicted and structural, from the pinned artifacts: laws/M0 (roles), results/M0 (statuses), results/M2/extracted_m1 (cones and statuses: 14 laws name the 8 modelled actions plus sendMessage and wait through step_<action>; L_tag_BVH, not run, has an empty cone), laws/M2/DERIVATION.json (entry points), results/M2 (statuses), spec/M2/facts/morph_header.extracted.json (walk functions, op origins, entries, revert lines), spec/M2/facts/morph_batch.go.extracted.json (call graph). Structural counts: stratum A reachable 103, masked 2, projection_carried 14, abstraction_carried 51, no_predicted_law 22; stratum B no_predicted_law 50.

9. Baseline statuses (pins): M0 5 PROVED (L_par_hdr_v0, L_par_hdr_v1, L_rt_go_v0, L_rt_go_v1, L_rt_go_v2), 3 REFUTED (L_par_hdr_v2, L_par_hdr_ssvh, L_dom_hdr); M1x as results/M2/differential.json 'extracted': 7 PROVED, 7 REFUTED, 1 UNKNOWN (L_tag_BVH); M2 12 laws: 6 PROVED, 4 UNKNOWN (L_sort_site_def_lci_356891e4, L_sort_site_l1messagequeuewithgaspriceoracle_325_f89daf17 and the two SORT-width laws), 2 REFUTED (L_sort_site_rollup_363_1fc7f88a, L_sort_site_rollup_636_e68daf06).

10. The diff sheet spec/M2/lib/mutation_diff_sheet_i60.md is diff_sheet.header followed, per mutant in id order, by '## <id> <operator> <variant> <file>:<line>:<col> <function>', a blank line and a ```diff block holding difflib.unified_diff(original lines, mutated lines, 'a/<file>', 'b/<file>', n=3, lineterm='') joined by newlines (tests_m2/test_mutation_adequacy_i60.py render_sheet is the reference). mutants_sha256 is the sha256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, separators ',' ':') of the mutants list.

11. seed 20261060 is fixed now. The catalog is exhaustive over the in-scope sites, so no sampling consumes it; every search uses the existing fixed seeds (holon.refute 20261010, the I16 and I20 corpora). A randomized step the build adds must take this seed.
12. Duplicate candidates (duplicates.rule): one group, A050 and A051 (the two cursor reads of the loop at Rollup.sol:489, I22's M046/M047 pattern).

threshold.source: docs/HUMAN_ANSWERS.md Q6 (0.80 of non-equivalent mutants in scope); docs/BUILD_PLAN.md §0.4

A.rule: Solidity: every FunctionDefinition and ModifierDefinition the I19 walker reaches from all actions of the adopted extracted rollup document (holon.frontends.solidity.transitions.walk_contract on spec/M2/lib/extract_rollup.json: Collector.reached, the set coverage_document counts for gen/M2/coverage.json; spec/M2/lib/derive_extracted.json adopts the document), plus every function of the header codec libraries (the units of the enc_sol and load_sol edges' op origins: BatchHeaderCodecV0, BatchHeaderCodecV1), OpenZeppelin units included (they compile into Rollup). Go: every function of each Go file that holds the implementation of a CODEC edge or domain predicate of a diagram under gen/M2/diagram/ (the facts' source[].file of those functions with lang go).

B.rule: Every other Go file of the pinned checkout that holds a function a committed spec/M2/facts/*.go.extracted.json lists under go.codecs.encoders, go.codecs.decoders or go.codecs.predicates (I18's codec recognition): extracted but not adopted. Every function of such a file is in scope.

strata.never: No scope or site rule mentions a law, a status or a result.

stillborn.error: go build: common/batch/encoding.go:5:2: "fmt" imported and not used

mstore_offset.pattern: a YulFunctionCall mstore or mstore8 whose first argument is a YulFunctionCall add with two arguments whose second is a decimal YulLiteral K (its source text is decimal digits)
mstore_offset.rewrite: the literal K becomes K-1 (variant -1, only when K >= 1) and K+1 (variant +1)

shl_width.pattern: a YulFunctionCall shl whose first argument is a decimal YulLiteral S
shl_width.rewrite: S becomes S-8 (variant -8) and S+8 (variant +8), each only when 0 < new value < 256

drop_delete.pattern: an ExpressionStatement whose expression is a UnaryOperation delete
drop_delete.rewrite: the statement, from 'delete' through its terminating semicolon, becomes {} followed by the newline characters of the replaced range (variant drop)

swap_cursor.pattern: an Identifier whose referencedDeclaration is a state variable of a pair in cursor_pairs and that is read: not the leftHandSide of an Assignment and not the operand of ++, -- or delete
swap_cursor.rewrite: the identifier becomes the other variable of its pair (variant swap)

cmp_boundary.pattern: a Solidity BinaryOperation with operator >= or > (Yul gt/lt are not matched); the site is the operator token between the operands' source ranges

cmp_boundary_mirror.plan: the mirrored flip of < and <= (new: F-A6)
cmp_boundary_mirror.pattern: a Solidity BinaryOperation with operator <= or <; the site is the operator token

mload_offset.pattern: a YulFunctionCall mload whose first argument is a YulFunctionCall add with two arguments whose second is a decimal YulLiteral K
mload_offset.rewrite: K becomes K-1 (variant -1, only when K >= 1) and K+1 (variant +1)

shr_width.pattern: a YulFunctionCall shr whose first argument is a decimal YulLiteral S
shr_width.rewrite: S becomes S-8 (variant -8) and S+8 (variant +8), each only when 0 < new value < 256

putuint64_offset.pattern: a call binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(x[K:], v): the first argument a slice expression with a decimal integer literal low bound K, no high and no max bound
putuint64_offset.rewrite: K becomes K-1 (variant -1, only when K >= 1) and K+1 (variant +1)

copy_offset.pattern: a call of the builtin copy(x[K:], y): the first argument a slice expression with a decimal integer literal low bound K, no high and no max bound
copy_offset.rewrite: K becomes K-1 (variant -1, only when K >= 1) and K+1 (variant +1)

drop_len_check.pattern: an if statement with no init and no else whose condition is a comparison (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=) of a call len(e) with a decimal integer literal or an identifier declared const in the same file, and whose body is exactly one return statement whose last result is a non-nil error value of the I18 go-errors-nonnil forms: an identifier (or selector) named Err..., errors.New(..) or fmt.Errorf(..)
drop_len_check.rewrite: the statement, from 'if' through its closing brace, becomes {} followed by the newline characters of the replaced range (variant drop)

go_slice_offset.pattern: a slice expression x[K1:K2] with decimal integer literal low and high bounds and no max bound that is read: not the first argument of copy or of a binary.BigEndian.Put* call
go_slice_offset.rewrite: the text K1:K2 becomes K1-1:K2-1 (variant -1, only when K1 >= 1) and K1+1:K2+1 (variant +1): the window moves, its width is kept

roles.doc: The M0 roles a mutant's edges name (projection roles). Solidity: role r is an edge of a mutant iff its function is in walk_functions of r's extracted edge in spec/M2/facts/morph_header.extracted.json (ok_sol is the load_sol edge). Go: role r is an edge iff its function is one of r's functions: the named functions and every function they call transitively through go.calls.edges with callee_kind 'analyzed' in spec/M2/facts/morph_batch.go.extracted.json. m0_law_roles: the functions each laws/M0 statement calls, with ok_go added to every statement that calls dec_go (dec_go is guarded by ok_go). A stratum-B or Rollup-only function has no edge.

M0.decided_by: python -m holon run --milestone M0 --facts <the projected header document> --no-registry

M1x.laws: the 15 laws/M1 laws over spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json (L_own_txspayload is over the hand Go facts and has no extracted decision path)
M1x.decided_by: python -m holon differential --milestone M2 (I20) over the mutant's rollup transitions document

M2.laws: laws/M2 as python -m holon derive --milestone M2 re-derives it over the mutant's documents
M2.facts: the documents each law names in 'facts' (spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json for SORT-site laws, spec/M2/facts/morph_rollup.extracted.json for SORT-width laws)

law_sets.own_input: A law's own decided input is the sha256 of the canonical JSON {statement, facts, cone}: statement = the law file it is decided from (laws/M0, laws/M1, or the run's laws/M2) with facts_sha256 removed; facts = {path: normalized sha256} of every document it is decided over; cone = {definition: sha256 of its BendTT kernel form} over the model it is decided on (holon.bindings.kernel_cone, the index results/<M>/deps.json is built from). Normalization removes only provenance: a document's top-level 'extraction' block. Canonical JSON: json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')), UTF-8. changed = differs from the baseline record's own input of the same law.
law_sets.carrying: A law whose own decided input equals the baseline's keeps the baseline status (decided: carried): determinism (same statement, facts and kernel forms give the same proof check and the same search). --no-carry decides every law; run --check reruns a sample with --no-carry and a disagreement is an error of the affected laws.
law_sets.matching: A law of a mutant run whose id is absent from the baseline is matched to the baseline law with the same (rule, subform, basis span) when exactly one exists (its record keeps the mutant id under that baseline law); otherwise it is a new law (baseline status 'absent').

predicted.rule: One rule for every operator. predicted(mutant) = M0 laws whose statement calls a role in the mutant's edges (roles.m0_law_roles: dec_go implies ok_go) + M1x laws whose recorded cone (results/M2/extracted_m1/<law>.json 'cone') names one of the mutant's actions (a cone names action a iff it holds the definition step_<a>) + M2 laws whose DERIVATION entry_points include one of the mutant's actions, laws derived only on the mutant included (their entry points read from the mutant run's laws/M2/DERIVATION.json).
predicted.actions: The actions of the adopted rollup document (33, receive included) whose walk reaches the mutant's function: the action's FunctionDefinition and every FunctionDefinition or ModifierDefinition reachable from it through Identifier, IdentifierPath, MemberAccess and ModifierInvocation references in solc 0.8.24's compact AST; their union equals the walker's reached set (computation item 2). Go functions have no action.

structural.doc: Which decision paths can see a mutant, from the committed artifacts alone, recorded before freezing so that every survivor is attributed mechanically (the run's survivor class is compared with it and every difference is reported).
structural.projection_read: A site is read by the projection of role r iff (Solidity) its operator is mstore_offset or shl_width and its function is an origin function of an op of an ok path of r (roles.solidity.<r>.origin_functions), or its operator is cmp_boundary or cmp_boundary_mirror and it lies in r's entry function or on a line one of r's revert paths names (roles.solidity.<r>.revert_lines); (Go) its function is one of r's functions. A site in a role's walk that the projection does not read cannot change the projected document: the projection reads ops, lengths and conditions on the role's input, not how the entry function computed the stored values.
structural.M0: reads: some predicted M0 law reads a projection-read site and is PROVED or UNKNOWN at baseline; masked: every such law is REFUTED at baseline; carried: predicted M0 laws exist but none reads a projection-read site; none: no predicted M0 law
structural.M1x: carried: predicted M1x laws exist; they are decided on m1_view, which changes only when a check reach of the same action appears or disappears at an M1 require's span, and no operator here adds or removes one; none: no predicted M1x law
structural.M2: carried: predicted M2 laws exist; SORT-site laws are decided on the hand model (their statement may change through the site: ref, their status cannot), SORT-width laws on the extracted model without a Reach predicate (UNKNOWN only); none: no predicted M2 law

classes.abstraction_carried: M0 is 'none' and M1x or M2 is 'carried'

kill_criterion.plan: A mutant is killed iff the obstruction predicted for its operator appears, localized to the mutated edge: a law moves to REFUTED, with a witness that replays on the mutant code, or a PROVED law loses its proof. A replay disagreement alone is recorded as "extraction defect detected", not as a kill. (BUILD_PLAN I22, verbatim)
kill_criterion.baseline: the same pipeline on the null mutant (the unmutated pinned files in a scratch copy); its statuses and own inputs are the reference
kill_criterion.K1: baseline PROVED or UNKNOWN (or the law is new: absent at baseline, derived on the mutant, its basis span inside a function the mutant mutates), mutant REFUTED with a Bend-checked counter-law for the recorded witness, and the recorded witness replays on the mutant code and does not replay on the original code (replay.hits)
kill_criterion.K2: baseline PROVED, mutant UNKNOWN, and all of: (a) the law's own decided input changed (law_sets.own_input); (b) the generator that proved it at baseline (the baseline record's accepted proof attempt) completed on the mutant and Bend rejected the proof: the attempt's exit_code is not null and its marker is 'SOME PROOFS FAIL'; (c) a code-level localized falsification exists: among the first replay_candidates candidates of the law's deterministic candidate space (refuter order), one makes the claim false on the mutant code and not false on the original code (replay.semantics). (a) and (b) without (c): proof_lost_unwitnessed, never a kill
kill_criterion.not_K2: a timeout of the proof check (exit_code null, '[timeout]'), LG.Unsupported, or a generator returning None on the mutant is a law-level error (retried once), never K2. A law PROVED at baseline and decided (run) on the mutant whose proof attempt by the baseline generator did not complete with a non-null exit code and the marker 'SOME PROOFS FAIL' is recorded as error (mutant status 'error'), never as UNKNOWN
kill_criterion.masked_obstruction: a predicted law REFUTED at baseline one of whose mutant model hits (up to replay_candidates, candidate order) replays on the mutant code and not on the original: reported, never a kill
kill_criterion.replay_disagreement: a law that moves to REFUTED (baseline PROVED, UNKNOWN or new) none of whose hits replays on the mutant code: the model's refutation is not the code's; it sets extraction_defect_detected and is never a kill
kill_criterion.baseline_finding: a law that moves to REFUTED whose hits replay on the mutant code only together with the original (every replaying hit replays on both): a finding the baseline model missed (whitepaper §9.6), never a kill and never an extraction defect
kill_criterion.unpredicted: a law outside the mutant's predicted set that satisfies K1 or K2: recorded per operator, never counted
kill_criterion.killed: some predicted law satisfies K1 or K2 on a decision path that completed
kill_criterion.errors: Errors are scoped to laws. A step that fails for a reason other than the law (an extraction, the projection, a set's run, a proof check timeout, a replay harness build) is retried once; if it fails again it marks only the laws it decides, or the law whose witness it replays, as error. A failed extraction of a document marks every law whose decision path reads it. outcome = killed if killed; else error if some predicted law is error; else survived. Failures on unpredicted laws and on channels are recorded only. Errors are counted per step.

replay.doc: The replay harness is an I60 deliverable (holon/mutate/replay.py, harness sources under replay/M2/mutation_i60/). It evaluates a law's claim, by claim and never by law id, at exact field values, on the code of a given source tree (a mutant's scratch copy or the unmutated one).
replay.m0: The statement's IR is evaluated bottom-up; each role call runs on the tree's own implementation: enc_sol through a Foundry harness generated from the tree's own source text (the statements of the role's entry function that its ok paths and revert paths come from, copied verbatim: the requires its revert paths name and the header build block up to the selected sink, the sink replaced by returning the bytes it hashes; every other value bound from the witness through the extracted ops' field map), ok_sol through the tree's Rollup._loadBatchHeader (a subclass, as I16's binding), enc_go_v0, enc_go_v1, ok_go and dec_go through a Go test in the tree's own package that recovers a panic per call; view is the specification (facts/morph_header.json functions.view). Each role runs in a fresh call frame: memory past the free pointer is zero, as on the deployed path.
replay.hits: The candidates are holon.refute's (holon.refute.candidates with the law's pins) in its order. The model hits are the candidates at which the compiled mutant model shows the claim false with every subterm defined (the refuter's own test), enumerated beyond the first, at most replay_candidates of them. Each is replayed on the mutant tree and on the original tree; the recorded witness is the first hit that replays on the mutant and not on the original, else the first hit. REFUTED needs a Bend-checked counter-law (holon.gen.proofs.counter) for the recorded witness.
replay.semantics: Per the functions' declared meanings (facts/morph_header.json 'meaning'): ok_sol is true iff the loader returns and false on any revert; ok_go is true on a nil error and false on a non-nil one; dec_go is None when validate() errs, else the getters' results in order (a getter that errs after validate() passed is absent, as I16's binding); enc_sol's revert on its own require has no value. An error or revert that is the function's value is not a violation. A role call with no value inside another call makes the candidate no execution (neither falsified nor confirmed: the model's undefined intermediate, holon.refute.subterms). A panic (Go panic, Solidity Panic 0x01-0x51 in a role the meaning gives no revert value) falsifies the claim. Trace laws (M1x, M2): a reverted step is a no-op; a Panic at the law's site falsifies it (the I15 panic_site replay); witnesses replay through holon.mreplay (M1x) and the I15 M2 replay on the tree's Rollup.
replay.both: a candidate that falsifies the claim on the mutant and on the original code is a baseline finding (kill_criterion.baseline_finding)

projection.doc: holon/mutate/project.py composes the holon-facts/0.1 header document the 8 laws/M0 statements are decided on, from extracted documents only (I22's projection, kept, with the additions below). types.Header and functions.view are copied from facts/morph_header.json (the laws' binder type and the specification). Every other function comes from its role's extracted document: enc_sol from the enc_sol edge, ok_sol from load_sol, enc_go_v0 and enc_go_v1 from the Go encoders, ok_go from the Go predicate's paths (true exactly where some nil-error path's conditions admit the input; a panicking path is not one), dec_go from the Go decoders guarded by ok_go.
projection.cells: A byte of an integer field written with width w (I17 N1: shl(8k, v) gives w = 32 - k; Go put/copy the field's own width) is aligned big-endian onto the Header field of width W: byte j of the w-byte value is byte W - w + j of the field, and a byte with W - w + j < 0 is the constant 0. A Solidity byte no op writes is undefined (A-dirty); a Go byte no op writes is 0.
projection.enc_sol: the extracted version bound is domain.version_le; per-version length and ops come from the ok paths at each version 0..version_le (length_by_version, ops with when). A revert condition on a field other than the version is not projected (listed in the document's assumptions as P-unprojected:<edge>).
projection.dec_go: each getter comes from its decoder function's nil-error paths (go.functions[fn].paths): one getter per (offset, width) read, with a when from the paths' condition on the version byte (version_ge when the version set is a threshold, else version_in). A getter whose decoder has no nil-error path that reads the input at constant offsets is undefined (every cell undefined).
projection.encoders: an encoder role whose function has no nil-error path (every path panics or errs), or whose cells the extraction leaves unknown, projects to an encoder whose unknown cells are undefined.
projection.extensions: Only additive extensions the M0 generator accepts (holon/facts.py, holon/gen/model.py: a when {version_in: [...]}, a field cell slice, an undefined cell or getter), so that facts/morph_header.json compiles to the same bytes as before (gate M0 G1 unchanged).
projection.output: gen/M2/mutation_i60/header.projected.json is the projection of the committed documents; holon mutate project --check reproduces it.

equivalence.definition: A mutant is equivalent iff, from every state the deployed code can reach, every call sequence through the public entry points gives the same observables on the original and on the mutant. Solidity: the entry points are those of Rollup, the deployed contract that the codec libraries and the inherited OpenZeppelin contracts compile into (the 33 actions of the adopted document, receive included); the observables are the success or revert of each call, its revert data, its return data, the emitted events (topics and data) and every storage slot. Go: the entry points are the exported functions and methods of the mutated package; the observables are the return values, the errors, whether a call panics, and every byte of every slice returned or written. Gas is not an observable. A difference only on states the code cannot reach is no difference. A mutant whose Rollup deployed bytecode equals the original's (tce) is equivalent.
equivalence.contradictions: A verdict 'equivalent' is contradicted when the mutant is killed by K1, has a code-level falsification (K2 (c), a masked obstruction, a baseline finding that replays on the mutant only), or has corpus_detected true. Each contradicted verdict is reported, and rate_non_equivalent is also reported with those verdicts reversed.

duplicates.rule: Duplicate candidates: two or more mutants of one statement-level operator (drop_delete, swap_cursor, cmp_boundary, cmp_boundary_mirror, drop_len_check) in the same file and line. The panel decides, for each candidate group, which mutants are semantic duplicates of the group's lowest id (the same observables on every reachable state); the summary reports the rates with each duplicate counted once beside the plain ones.

tce.rule: Trivial compiler equivalence (computation item 6): a Solidity mutant whose Rollup deployed bytecode (solc 0.8.24, optimizer off, cancun, metadata bytecodeHash none, no CBOR) equals the original's. Equivalent by construction; the panel records it so.

channels.doc: Detection channels never decide a kill. Each record lists exactly its runs. Stratum B has none.
channels.i20_step: The baseline and every stratum-A Solidity mutant: I20's step harness (holon fragments with I20's binding replay/M2/fragments.json and --disagreements in scratch) runs the baseline run's corpus (its traces and fork steps) on the mutant contract against the mutant's extracted rollup model. new_disagreements: the disagreements the baseline's run does not have; corpus_differences: the step ids where the mutant contract's observables (status, revert key, touched storage slots, logs) differ from the original contract's on the same corpus. A completed run covers at least 2432 steps (the m1 source alone).
channels.i16_edge: The baseline, every stratum-A Go mutant and every stratum-A Solidity mutant whose edges are non-empty: I16's per-edge refinement of the mutant's projected document against the mutant code on I16's per-edge corpus (new_disagreements as above; corpus_differences null). A completed run covers at least one step.
channels.flags: extraction_defect_detected: true when some law is a replay disagreement or some run reports a new disagreement; null when neither and some run is incomplete; false otherwise. corpus_detected: for a stratum-A Solidity mutant, whether the completed i20_step run's corpus_differences is non-empty; null when that run is incomplete and for every other mutant. A harness that exits without a result (a panic, a build failure) leaves its run incomplete, with its error.

rules: extraction_gap (gap_stage frontend): no extracted document changed (normalized)
rule_gap (rule_gap_kind no_law): the predicted set is empty
extraction_gap (gap_stage model): some document changed and no predicted law's own decided input changed
masked: every predicted law whose own decided input changed is REFUTED at baseline
proof_lost_unwitnessed: some predicted law satisfies K2 (a) and (b) and none satisfies (c)
rule_gap (rule_gap_kind law_unmoved): otherwise (a predicted law that is not REFUTED at baseline was re-decided on a changed input and kept its status)

reporting.rates: per stratum (A, B and all): mutants, killed, killed_k1, equivalent, killed_equivalent, errors, rate_all {num, den, value} = killed / mutants, rate_non_equivalent {num, den, value} = (killed and not equivalent) / (not equivalent), meets_threshold = 5 * num >= 4 * den for stratum A's rate_non_equivalent (null for B and all)
reporting.k1_only: per stratum: rate_non_equivalent counting only mutants some predicted law of which satisfies K1
reporting.by_operator: per stratum and operator: mutants, killed, killed_k1, equivalent, errors, unpredicted (mutants with an unpredicted obstruction), masked (mutants with a masked obstruction), proof_lost_unwitnessed
reporting.by_family: per stratum and law family (PAR-codec: L_par_hdr_*; PAR-round-trip: L_rt_go_*; PAR-domain: L_dom_hdr; M1x:<rule>; M2:<rule>/<subform>): predicted = mutants whose predicted set holds a law of the family, killed = mutants a law of the family kills. Every law entry of a record carries its family, so the rates are recomputed from the records
reporting.detection: per stratum: mutants with some localized obstruction (killed, an unpredicted obstruction or a masked obstruction) / mutants
reporting.dedup: per stratum: rate_all and rate_non_equivalent with every adjudicated duplicate removed
reporting.contradicted: equivalence.contradictions, and rate_non_equivalent of stratum A with the contradicted verdicts reversed
reporting.structural_agreement: per structural class: the survivor classes it received (survivor_classes.expected_from_structure)
reporting.metric: results/M2/metrics.json 'mutation_adequacy' (whitepaper §13; §12.1 Sensitivity): {source: the summary path, threshold: 0.8, rate_all, rate_non_equivalent, meets_threshold} of stratum A; the metric leaves not_applicable (I23 reads it)
reporting.obstruction_rates: per stratum: unpredicted_rate = mutants with some unpredicted obstruction / mutants; masked_rate = mutants with some masked obstruction / mutants (beside the per-operator counts)

adjudication.delegation: The human delegated the catalog sign-off and the equivalence verdicts to independent fresh agents (docs/HUMAN_ANSWERS.md, answers delegated to the lead, 2026-10-13; docs/iterations/I22.md). The lead does not sign off a catalog it drafted.
adjudication.forbidden: Neither step's agents read spec/M2/predictions.json key I60, prompts/I60_mutation_replacement.md, tests_m2/test_mutation_adequacy_i60.py, docs/iterations/, or any I60 result; each lists the forbidden files it touched (names only).
adjudication.review: Step 1, catalog review: two fresh agents, one per lens (fairness: what the catalog counts and leaves out; soundness: the kill criterion, the replay semantics, the error scope), each reading this instrument in full and recomputing the sites from the pinned checkout. Output docs/iterations/I60_catalog_review.json: {"what", "who", "delegation", "instrument": {"path", "sha256"}, "verdict", "reviews": {"fairness" | "soundness": {"sign_off": bool, "blocking": [...], "advisory": [...], "checked", "forbidden_files_touched": [...]}}}. Signed off iff both lenses sign off with no blocking finding. If not, nothing runs and a replacement is preregistered under a new key.
adjudication.panel: Step 2, blind equivalence panel, after a signed-off review: per file group (codec libraries; Rollup.sol; the OpenZeppelin units; common/batch/batch_header.go; the stratum-B Go files), two independent judges (one reasoning from the source, one building distinguishing scenarios and running them where it can), then one adversarial refuter who attacks every mutant at least one judge calls equivalent and every duplicate candidate group. They see only a blind folder: the diff sheet trimmed to the definition, the operators and the mutant sections, and the pinned sources. A mutant is equivalent iff the refuter confirms it; disagreement or doubt is not equivalent; a tce mutant is equivalent. Every tool call is audited for reads outside the blind folder.
adjudication.file: spec/M2/equivalent_mutants_i60.json, committed alone after the review and before any result: {"adjudication_version": "holon-equivalent-mutants/0.2", "instrument": {"path", "sha256"}, "mutants_sha256", "diff_sheet_sha256", "review": {"path", "sha256"}, "adjudicator": "delegated_panel", "delegation": {"decision", "panel", "procedure", "blindness_audit"}, "verdicts": {"<id>": {"equivalent": bool, "reason": str (non-empty when equivalent), "duplicate_of": null | "<id>", "panel": {"judges": [bool, bool], "refuter_confirmed": bool | null}}}} with every mutant id exactly once.
adjudication.panel_record: Optional: the panel's full record (each judge's and the refuter's output, the blindness audit) at docs/iterations/I60_equivalence_panel.json, an I60 outcome path, first committed after the adjudication and never in its commit

header: # I60 mutant diff sheet: equivalent-mutant adjudication (HOLON M2, auditor A1, replacement catalog)
Generated from the frozen I60 instrument spec/M2/lib/mutation_catalog_i60.json (its "mutants" list, canonical JSON
sha256 eccefd69d69138492c1a387afddba644b84767059cde10163d5044fcaf3dc24a)
and the pinned morph-l2/morph checkout at 3e44e795586af3e11285b603ab642c67823add51 (OpenZeppelin units from config/holon.json
replay.sol_deps). `python -m holon mutate sheet` reproduces this file byte for byte. It shows each of the 242 mutants
(192 in stratum A, ids A..., 50 in stratum B, ids B...) as a unified diff with 3 lines of context, and nothing
else: no prediction, no outcome. No mutant has been run.
## What the panel decides
For every mutant: is it EQUIVALENT to the original program? Decide from this sheet and the pinned sources alone.
Do not read spec/M2/predictions.json key I60, prompts/I60_mutation_replacement.md,
tests_m2/test_mutation_adequacy_i60.py, docs/iterations/ or any I60 result: they hold the predictions.
A mutant is equivalent iff, from every state the deployed code can reach, every call sequence through the public
entry points gives the same observables on the original and on the mutant. Solidity: the entry points are those of
Rollup, the deployed contract that the codec libraries and the inherited OpenZeppelin contracts compile into (its
external and public functions and receive); the observables are the success or revert of each call, its revert
data, its return data, the emitted events (topics and data) and every storage slot. Go: the entry points are the
exported functions and methods of the mutated package; the observables are the return values, the errors, whether
a call panics, and every byte of every slice returned or written. Gas is not an observable. A mutant that differs
only on states the code cannot reach is equivalent; one that differs on any reachable state is not. When unsure,
say not equivalent. Every equivalent verdict needs a reason.
These mutants leave Rollup's deployed bytecode unchanged (solc 0.8.24, optimizer off, cancun, no metadata): A110, A111, A112, A113, A121, A122.
They are equivalent by construction.
Duplicate candidates (one operator, one statement): {A050, A051}. For each group, say which mutants give the same
observables as the group's lowest id on every reachable state.
The verdicts go to spec/M2/equivalent_mutants_i60.json (the format is in the instrument's "adjudication" field),
committed alone, after the catalog review and before any run. Equivalent mutants leave the denominator of the
non-equivalent kill rate; the rate over all mutants is reported too.
## Operators
- mstore_offset (-1, +1): the literal offset K of an inline-assembly mstore/mstore8(add(p, K), v) becomes K-1 or K+1.
- shl_width (-8, +8): the literal shift S of an inline-assembly shl(S, v) becomes S-8 or S+8.
- drop_delete (drop): a `delete x;` statement becomes the empty block `{}`.
- swap_cursor (swap): a read of lastCommittedBatchIndex becomes lastFinalizedBatchIndex, and vice versa.
- cmp_boundary (flip): a Solidity `>=` becomes `>`, and `>` becomes `>=`.
- cmp_boundary_mirror (flip): a Solidity `<=` becomes `<`, and `<` becomes `<=`.
- mload_offset (-1, +1): the literal offset K of an inline-assembly mload(add(p, K)) becomes K-1 or K+1.
- shr_width (-8, +8): the literal shift S of an inline-assembly shr(S, v) becomes S-8 or S+8.
- putuint64_offset (-1, +1): the literal K of binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(x[K:], v) becomes K-1 or K+1.
- copy_offset (-1, +1): the literal K of copy(x[K:], y) becomes K-1 or K+1.
- drop_len_check (drop): an `if` comparing len(..) with a constant whose body only returns an error becomes `{}`.
- go_slice_offset (-1, +1): a read slice x[K1:K2] with literal bounds becomes x[K1-1:K2-1] or x[K1+1:K2+1].
Every replacement keeps the file's line count, so line numbers in the diffs are the pinned file's.
